truss 报价出来了,一共 8,400 新币,包含运输和安装。

花艺部分:主台的花明天下午送到,侧台的要后天。另外增加两个花柱,每个 450。
We'll have the test print ready by next Tuesday.
cases.note: Relative weekday resolution. Model must use sent_at + weekday from context.

cases.message: 后天早上把地毯铺好。
cases.note: 后天 = day after tomorrow. Tests relative-date arithmetic in Chinese.

cases.message: Ah Seng here — can deliver the LED screen tomorrow morning lah, no problem one.
cases.note: Sentence-final particles 'lah' and 'one' (emphasis/affirmation) around a plain forward commitment, date-only relative resolution.

cases.message: The truss frame done already lor, can collect anytime after 3pm today.
cases.note: 'Already' as a completion marker (not a time word) plus sentence-final 'lor' — tests that the model reports this as confirm (already done), not commit, and doesn't misread 'already' as part of a date.

cases.message: Eh can you chase the venue for our loading bay access or not? We stuck outside since 10am.
cases.note: The 'X or not?' question pattern — tests it's read as a query asking the recipient to act, not a commitment, and that no due_at is fabricated from '10am' (that's describing the current problem, not a deadline).

cases.message: Wah the seafood cost went up already sia, now $18 per pax instead of $15.
cases.note: Exclamatory 'wah' + sentence-final 'sia' around a price renegotiation — tests the interjection/particle doesn't get mistaken for content, and the new (not old) amount is extracted.

cases.message: Bloomworks here — flowers for the main stage confirm already, we deliver 23 Jun morning can.
cases.note: Bare-verb future tense ('we deliver' meaning 'we will deliver') plus sentence-final 'can' as an affirmation particle, around an explicit calendar date rather than a relative one.

cases.message: While we're on Golden Sound & Light — can someone confirm the Stage Power Distribution Board ($6,200) is still tracking for the 29th?
cases.note: vendor-attribution-task.md's real reported bug, verbatim. This is an *internal* Mattermost channel — the sender (Farah Rahman, Finance) is never the vendor; the vendor (Golden Sound & Light) is only named inside the message text. Tests that counterparty_name is extracted from content, not left null / filled with the sender. 'party' here is deliberately the human sender, not the vendor — app/ledger/extractor.py resolves the actual vendor party for team_collaboration channels, this harness only scores the model's own extraction.

cases.message: Heads up — Vertex Fabrication just confirmed the truss frame is ready, they'll deliver it tomorrow morning.
cases.note: Internal Mattermost channel naming a vendor already in project_context.vendors (Vertex Fabrication) — the match-against-known-vendors path, distinct from IC01's unmatched-vendor path. Sender (Marcus Lim, Producer) is internal staff relaying what the vendor said, not the vendor.

cases.message: Twin's flagging this as touching the critical path — rehearsal is booked right after install, so a 2hr slip here eats directly into that buffer. No slack left if anything else moves.
cases.note: extraction-tuning-task.md failure mode 1, verbatim. Internal staff discussing the *consequence* of an already-captured AV-delay commitment (Ah Seng's 2hr slip, see T01) — no offer/commit/confirm/quote/approve/revoke/renegotiate/query is made here, so per CLAUDE.md's 'one commitment per distinct promise' this message should extract zero commitments. Both qwen2.5:14b and claude-haiku-4-5 previously over-split this into a standalone 'rehearsal buffer' commitment. Deliberately given NO ledger_context, unlike CD02: this message makes no request at all, so it is the case that proves the model does not invent a commitment out of pure discussion even with nothing to point at.

cases.message: Noted. As long as it's contained to today's install window we're fine — client walkthrough isn't until next week. Can we get written confirmation the 4pm start still lands before end of day?
cases.note: extraction-tuning-task.md failure mode 1, verbatim, WITH the ledger context a real capture would have had. The label was deliberately changed from the context-free count:0 it was first written with. Without context this message is indistinguishable from S03 — both are the sender asking the recipient to do something, which prompt.txt's own `query` rule says to extract — so count:0 was unsatisfiable from the message text alone, and could only ever have been met by a rule that also broke S03 (CLAUDE.md: 'check the label before changing the prompt'). The fact that makes it not-new lives in an earlier message, so it is supplied the way production supplies it: as an already-logged commitment the model can point at. Correct behaviour is one item linked to C1, which app/ledger/extractor.py persists as an Evidence row on the existing commitment — creating no new ledger row, so the business outcome (no invented checklist item) is the one this case was written to protect, while the chase itself is still recorded.

cases.message: Good. One more — Ah Seng's LED screen install and Vertex's aluminum frame delivery + test print are still sitting as proposed, no confirmed dates yet. Don't want those turning into last-minute like the Golden Sound & Light delay.
cases.note: extraction-tuning-task.md failure mode 2, verbatim — the under-splitting half of the reported bug, which the suite had no case for at all. claude-haiku-4-5 merged this into ONE commitment ('LED screen install and aluminum frame delivery with test print confirmation'), welding two different vendors' two different deliverables into a single record. Deliberately given NO ledger_context: this case measures whether the model splits by counterparty when everything it needs is already in the message (the PDF's own 'does the AI have enough information? Yes'), so mixing in the relates_to path would stop it isolating that. act_type is deliberately not labelled — internal staff flagging two stalled items is a genuine escalate/query borderline, and pinning it would make this case fail for a reason unrelated to the splitting behaviour it exists to measure.
